newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to host ICO, robusta producers' meeting.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to host ICO, robusta producers' meeting.

text.p: Indonesia will host the executive board meeting of the International Coffee Organisation (ICO) on the resort island of Bali from February 3 to 5.
The meeting will be followed by separate gatherings of coffee producers from the Asia-Pacific region and Robusta producers on February 6.
Industry sources said the ICO meeting would examine developments in cooperation between consumers and producers, new membership and the growing demand for speciality coffee.
They said no agenda had been set yet for the meetings of the Asia-Pacific coffee producers, and Robusta producers.

African producers are trying to get the 14 members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) to cut exports by 2.5 million 60-kg bags in the first half of this year in a bid to bolster Robusta prices.
Oesman Soedargo, chairman of the Association of Indonesian Coffee Exporters said on Thursday Indonesia was "open to discussion" on the proposal.
Paian Nainggolan, Indonesia's representative to the ACPC, had indicated that Indonesia would not back the African move.
The ACPC will hold an emergency meeting in Brazil this week to discuss, among others, the African proposal.
"If the issue (African move) is settled at the Brazil meeting, there'll be nothing much left to discuss at the Robusta producers' meeting (in Bali)," one industry source said.

Indonesia, the world's third largest coffee producer after Brazil and Colombia, is reluctant to back the African proposal because its trade rival Vietnam is not an ACPC member and does not have to cut exports if the plan gets ACPC support.
